final_candidates.decision_summary: Substitution of the conserved Trp59 with charged aspartate severely disrupts the cofactor/substrate binding pocket, resulting in complete loss of enzymatic activity.
Alanine ablation of the strictly conserved catalytic Arg157 eliminates critical catalytic interactions while preserving overall fold integrity.
Charge reversal at active-site Arg157 induces severe electrostatic repulsion in the active site, effectively abolishing catalytic turnover.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 loss-of-function mutations are firmly established by convergent evolutionary and pathogenicity evidence.

history.rationale: Asp223 is the conserved catalytic proton donor/acceptor; alanine substitution directly abolishes catalytic turnover while maintaining fold integrity.
AlphaMissense scores D223A as ambiguous (0.442), suggesting possible residual activity or structural accommodation.
Displays intermediate to low pathogenicity, indicating incomplete loss of function.
Isosteric removal of the catalytic carboxylate at Asp223 disables essential proton transfer, yielding a catalytically inactive enzyme.
Predicted as benign (0.156) by AlphaMissense, suggesting it is unlikely to reliably achieve complete loss of function.
Rejected due to low pathogenicity score (0.156) and relatively high PLM plausibility (0.05), indicating a benign/tolerated neutral variant rather than LOF.

rejection.reason: Rejected due to low pathogenicity score (0.156) and relatively high PLM plausibility (0.05), indicating a benign/tolerated neutral variant rather than LOF.

history.rationale: Clinically established severe deficiency mutation in the active site that drastically reduces MTHFR catalytic activity to below detectable levels.
R157Q has lower AlphaMissense pathogenicity (0.629) compared to R157A/E, retaining polar character that may partially rescue binding.
Glutamine substitution retains polarity and partial hydrogen bonding, showing lower pathogenicity proxy score than alanine or glutamate.
Neutralization of active-site residue Arg157 disrupts critical electrostatic interactions essential for cofactor/substrate binding and catalysis.
R157 is critical for substrate binding, and R157A yields an outstanding AlphaMissense score of 0.973 without creating major steric clashing.
Ablation of key active site/cofactor-binding Arg157 to alanine has near-zero sequence plausibility and very high pathogenic LOF likelihood.
Charge reversal at active-site Arg157 creates severe electrostatic repulsion, abolishing substrate/cofactor binding and activity.
Charge inversion at substrate-coordinating R157 (0.963 AlphaMissense) effectively abolishes catalytic activity.
Charge reversal at Arg157 severely disrupts substrate/cofactor binding with high predicted LOF score and zero ESM-1v tolerance.
Trp59 provides essential aromatic stacking for the FAD cofactor; alanine substitution severely disrupts FAD binding and eliminates activity.
W59A disrupts FAD cofactor stacking (0.895 AlphaMissense), though slight homolog tolerance decreases relative priority.
Remains an effective loss-of-function candidate but ranks below the more disruptive aspartate substitution W59D.
Introducing a charged aspartate into the hydrophobic FAD-binding pocket at position 59 abolishes cofactor binding and enzymatic function.
W59D exhibits the highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity score (0.987), strongly predicting severe disruption of FAD binding and enzyme inactivation.
Extremely high pathogenic prediction from AlphaMissense coupled with a near-zero ESM-1v plausibility score strongly supports complete loss of catalytic function.
Introducing a bulky charged residue directly adjacent to catalytic Asp223 sterically and electrostatically disrupts the catalytic loop conformation.
G221D introduces a bulky negative charge near the catalytic loop with high predicted pathogenicity (0.845).
Known clinically severe variant leading to enzyme instability and activity loss, though slightly below the top catalytic residue mutations.
Proline substitution adjacent to catalytic Asp223 distorts the active-site beta-strand geometry, severely abolishing enzyme activity.
A222P introduces helix-breaking proline at the known thermolabile A222 site, showing very high predicted pathogenicity (0.953).
Introduction of proline at position 222 causes structural disruption near the thermolabile locus, yielding high pathogenicity and zero PLM support.
Glu123 is a conserved active-site loop acidic residue; mutation to alanine impairs active-site organization and catalytic competence.
E123A shows moderate pathogenicity (0.689), functioning well as an active site disruptor but with lower certainty than top candidates.
Moderate pathogenicity proxy score and PLM intolerance, remaining in the mid-tier of candidates.
